newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Riksbank sets new pattern for monetary policy. [corrected 16:20 gmt]
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Riksbank sets new pattern for monetary policy. [corrected 16:20 gmt]

text.p: Sweden's Riksbank signalled a new direction in monetary policy on Thursday as it lowered its deposit and lending rates by 50 basis points and trimmed 25 basis points from its key repo rate.

Departing from its long-established pattern of adjusting the repo rate every other Tuesday, the Riksbank said it would cut the repo rate to 4.60 percent at next week's reverse repurchase tender and keep it there for the following three operations.

"We don't want a focus every Tuesday, but on the information that is published. It's not the pattern but the incoming (economic) information we should be looking at," Riksbank governor Urban Backstrom told a news conference.

With the rate of inflation in Sweden falling to 0.2 percent, its lowest level in four decades, the Riksbank has had free hands to pursue an aggressive monetary policy to stimulate the country's fragile economy.
The repo rate been cut 22 times this year, falling over four percentage points from its January level of 8.91 percent.

Thursday's move brought the deposit and lending rates, the floor and ceiling of the central bank's interest rate corridor, down to 4.25 percent and 5.75 percent respectively, leaving room for more cuts in the repo rate.
However, Backstrom said room for further belt-loosening was limited, even suggesting that the rate might remain where it is.

"The scenario is not unambiguous," Backstrom said. "It means that we need additional time to follow and analyse incoming information. The conclusion of the judgements made could also be an unchanged repo rate."

Even so, the Riksbank maintains its view that inflationary pressure is by no means out of control, and that consumer price increases are likely to remain within the central bank's one to three percent target range.
"The decisions are based on the assessment that the outlook for inflation in the coming years remains in line with the (two percent) inflation target," the bank said in a statement.
"The future monetary stance will depend on new information and how it relates to the analysis in the Riksbank's latest (September) inflation report."
The lowering of the rate corridor was widely tipped by analysts, but the decision to cut the repo rate initially sent a positive ripple of surprise through the market.
However, the mood of the market turned sour as news of the bank's more cautious stance emerged in the afternoon.

After an initial seven basis point fall to 7.17 percent, the yield on the nine-year government bond crept up to 7.20 percent as the market found itself wrong-footed by what some players saw as conflicting signals.

Even so, analysts said the change of tactics was logical in the light of recent comments by deputy Riksbank governor Lars Heikensten that monetary policy should not be expected to conform to a pre-determined pattern.
"The board is indicating more clearly the course of future monetary policy, it has taken a firmer grip," Swedbank analyst Ake Gustafsson said.
